Problem Statement:
🐛 Fix support for functools wraps and partial combined, for async and regular functions and classes in path operations and dependencies

🐛 Fix support for functools wraps and partial combined, for async and regular functions and classes in path operations and dependencies

This also uses and extends the tests created by @YuriiMotov :raised_hands: 

Should fix / related to: https://github.com/fastapi/fastapi/issues/14444

The new tests simulate the multiple combinations of how decorators could affect dependencies and path operation functions (endpoints).

The logic to analyze if a function is an async, generator, async generator,  callable instance, etc. now also checks and unwraps and extracts partials in all those levels.

The main case is when the callable is an _async_ something (function, generator, etc) because then it needs to be awaited.

But the original function could be async or not, the wrapper could be async or not. if either is async, then it has to be awaited, no matter if the other is not async. So, analyzing only the last point in the chain is not enough, it's necessary to analyze the function but also the wrapper.

This PR implements and tests all that, all those combinations.

turns.reply: The dependency analysis only inspects the unwrapped end of the chain, so an async wrapper around a sync function (or the reverse) gets misclassified. I'll make each check walk every level of the `__wrapped__`/`partial` chain and return true if any level matches.

         return False
 
     @cached_property
+    def _unwrapped_calls(self) -> List[Any]:
+        """
+        All the callables in the wrapping chain (functools.wraps via
+        `__wrapped__`, and functools.partial via `.func`), outermost first.
+        """
+        if self.call is None:
+            return []  # pragma: no cover
+        chain: List[Any] = []
+        current: Any = self.call
+        seen: set = set()
+        while current is not None and id(current) not in seen:
+            seen.add(id(current))
+            chain.append(current)
+            if isinstance(current, partial):
+                current = current.func
+            elif hasattr(current, "__wrapped__"):
+                current = current.__wrapped__
+            else:
+                break
+        return chain

+            return check(obj)

+        dunder_call = getattr(obj, "__call__", None)  # noqa: B004

turns.reply:
I changed `fastapi/dependencies/models.py` so that the async, generator, and async-generator checks for dependencies inspect every level of the wrapper chain, not just the innermost callable. The patch is submitted (1 file, 3252 bytes).

The chain is built by following `functools.partial(.func)` and `__wrapped__`, and each check returns true if any level matches. An async wrapper around a sync function, a sync wrapper around an async function, and a partial over an async function are all detected as coroutines. The sync cases still come out as non-coroutines.

Verification was limited: a small script confirmed the coroutine classification for those cases, and `tests/test_dependency_cache.py`, `tests/test_dependency_class.py` and `tests/test_dependency_partial.py` pass (24 tests). I did not run the full suite or check the generator and async-generator paths directly. The path-operation side is not separately verified either; I only changed the dependency model.
